text: BraviSEAmo! (ブラヴィッシーモ! Buravisshiimo!) was a nighttime water show at Tokyo DisneySea that ran from July 17, 2004, to November 13, 2010, replacing the earlier show DisneySea Symphony and being succeeded by a new version of Fantasmic! in 2011. The show was directed by Yves Pépin from ECA2 and featured minimal dialogue, relying instead on an orchestral score composed, orchestrated, and conducted by Gavin Greenaway, who had previously worked on IllumiNations: Reflections of Earth and Tapestry of Nations. The music was recorded at Paramount Scoring Stage M in Hollywood, California by Tom Vicari and mixed and mastered at O'Henry Sound Studios and Digital Domain Mastering, respectively. Bellisea's vocals were performed by Lisbeth Scott, and the theme song "Swept Away" was composed by Greenaway with lyrics by Donna Elaine Miller, sung by Miller and Rick Logan. While the show's dialogue was in Japanese, an English version of "Swept Away" was performed during the main show, and a Japanese-language version was created for use only during the Tokyo DisneySea Season of Hearts promotion from February 14 to March 14, 2007, and included on the BraviSEAmo! Complete album released in 2007. The show was performed once daily at 7:25 pm and took place on the lagoon of Mediterranean Harbor. It featured water, pyrotechnic, and firework effects, beginning with darkening lights and a pre-show musical portion with mist, followed by a horn call and a large pentagram formed by spotlights. Mickey Mouse entered in an aquatic chariot pulled by sea horses, dressed as a sea prince with a flowing robe, a crown of large golden tasseled feathers, and a trident, and welcomed the audience "to this world of magic," launching low-level fireworks. The narrative introduced a Water Spirit named Bellisea and a Fire Spirit named Prometeo, who lived in separate worlds and never met. Fountains formed water patterns to the music of the Water Spirit Bellisea, after which Bellisea appeared as a woman made of flowing water on a barge. An aggressive drumbeat and thunder followed as fireworks launched from Mount Prometheus, and Prometeo emerged as a mechanical phoenix with fire burning in rune-like shapes and flames from his wings. Bellisea then reawakened and began singing, prompting Prometeo to join in, and as they approached each other, the fountains erupted, their voices harmonized, and the two spirits symbolically fell in love. Prometeo's fiery wings transformed into curtains of sparks and his body sparkled with blue lights, while Bellisea launched fireworks from her barge. More fireworks erupted from Mount Prometheus and the lagoon, and Mickey exclaimed "Bravissimo! Ha ha!" before the show concluded with the ending song "Swept Away." The show's development began in 2002, after Oriental Land Company show producer Koichi Sasamoto and his team contacted ECA2 and Yves Pépin, who had previously designed the Eiffel Tower Millennium Show and Magical Sentosa. John Haupt served as producer and Thomas Tryon as production manager. The concept was developed in France, with Bruno Corsini as lighting designer and Barbizon Lighting supplying the equipment, and Troy Starr as systems integrator. Christophe Berthonneau of Groupe F Pyrotechnie designed the fireworks, using 40 flame-throwers integrated into the Prometeo design. The team visited a fireworks factory in Valencia, Spain, where they built and tested a full-scale Prometeo prototype, calibrating flame-throwers and testing launchers. After returning to Japan, Sasamoto oversaw the construction of the show-use Prometeo, manufactured by a precision machinery firm, which was tested for two months in water and installed in a 6-meter deep pit in the lagoon. The show-use Prometeo was 14 meters tall and 32 meters wide, and Bellisea was 11 meters tall. The project included several technical firsts: it was the first to use a Global Positioning System (GPS) to track four fountain barges and two large barges for accurate positioning, and the first to use a wireless LAN for all show communications, including lighting, fountains, and pyrotechnics, due to the absence of competing radio frequencies at the Tokyo Disney Resort. The lighting used DMX512 protocols, with Prometeo's rig including 3,000 waterproof Japanese-made LEDs, 250 Birket Strobe-Brik strobes, and 2 narrow spot PAR lamps, all encased in stainless steel and waterproofed for underwater operation. Shore-based lighting included 42 Halto/Griven Rainbows, 42 Griven Everest CYM MSD700 fixtures, 10 Space Cannon Ireos Pro VHT 7 kW color-changing fixtures, Coemar NAT 2.5 kW and 4 kW fixtures in Tempest enclosures, 380 Pace PARs, 130 Hydrel waterproof PAR64s with custom dichroic filters, and Aqua Signal marine floodlights, controlled by Electrol Engineering D625dx dimmers and managed via a High End Systems Wholehog III console. Daily preparation began at 1 am with 16 pyrotechnicians installing 850 fireworks, concluding at 12 pm, and 60 crew members were trained, with 40 actively involved in each performance. Each of the four fountain barges had a driver, and the Chariot and Bellisea barges each had a driver and a spotter. The total development and production cost of BraviSEAmo! was 3 billion yen (nearly $37 million in 2011 dollars).
